articles.title: Yankees captain Aaron Judge makes his wife's marathon day even more special
articles.summary: Aaron Judge is used to being the center of attention in New York. During the baseball season, the Yankees captain draws crowds with towering home runs, clutch hits and the kind of power that has made him one of Major League Baseball's biggest stars. On Sunday, however, Judge was perfectly happy to let someone else take the spotlight. With the MLB offseason underway, the 6-foot-7 slugger showed up to cheer on his wife, Samantha, as she ran the New York City Marathon. And when she spotted her family along the course, the race briefly turned into a special family moment — with the couple's young daughter, Nora Rose, adding an especially sweet touch. Wearing sunglasses and a Yankees pullover, Judge was hard to miss among the spectators. His height alone made him stand out, but his role as a supportive husband and father made the moment more memorable than his unmistakable presence in the crowd.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark turns Halloween into a night of scares with a simple mask and a few tricks
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark traded a big Halloween party for a night at home, where she decided to scare trick-or-treaters with nothing more than a mask. The Fever star managed to send some of the younger children running, but the older kids weren't nearly as impressed by her costume and seemed harder to frighten. None of them realized the person behind the mask was Clark herself, something that might have made their reactions a little more enthusiastic. Aliyah Boston, meanwhile, gave Clark's Halloween prank her seal of approval. She was even cozier than her teammate, relaxing in bed when Clark called her on FaceTime, clearly excited to show off her scary mask. The Fever teammates appear to be enjoying a quieter offseason after a WNBA season that didn't go entirely as planned.

articles.title: Simone Biles takes on a terrifying challenge 100 feet above the ground for charity
articles.summary: Olympic champion Simone Biles took on one of the wildest challenges of her career, but this time, it was for a good cause. The gymnast teamed up with MrBeast to walk across narrow beams suspended 100 feet above the ground, facing a challenge that tested even her balance skills. While MrBeast had to cross a beam just 4 inches wide, Biles had only 1.5 inches of space beneath her feet, less than half the width of the balance beams she normally competes on. The challenge offered $250,000 for charity, and Biles chose to support foster children, a cause close to her heart after spending part of her childhood in foster care. After making it safely to the other side, the Olympic medalist celebrated the achievement in style.
